# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: How to order the phases of an implementation or migration plan so nothing stalls mid-run — front-load the out-of-band setup, collapse the review gates into one stacked-PR pass, leave only executable steps — and how to keep its tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use when writing or reviewing a migration plan or a phased implementation plan, and when working through one's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. design*: F17 reframed (heartbeat interval < leash replaces leash >
    every work bound), the `timeout-minutes ≤ leash` run cap retired (§6),
    and the item's timeline stays live through long work. One mechanism
    serves recovery and visibility.
16. **The tick never waits on a drain** (§10) — *changed the design*: the
    double-tick serialization scopes to the tick alone; executor work runs
    outside that concurrency group, or the heartbeat's legal long runs would
    starve the hourly tick behind the platform's queueing.
17. **The occupancy capacity model** (§10): a drain's throughput is its
    serial work-step occupancy, so `maxItems` and executor width are the
    primary capacity parameters; self-re-dispatch (`workflow_dispatch`, one
    of the two events a `GITHUB_TOKEN` can fire) is the drain-until-empty
    shape; the oldest-first fairness exposure is named and accepted at
    today's scale.
18. **The terminal comment is the durable record** (§6.5): the
    `claudinite-task-exec` record and every artifact the work created land on
    the item at close — Actions logs expire, and for agentless runs (the
    majority, under this review's premise) the item is the only durable trace.
19. **F1 reopened — readiness re-checks at close** (§9), amending decision 8
    in siting, not principle: whoever closes an item readies its dependents in
    code and a drain follows; the tick stays the backstop. (S33, S4.)

    same day*: first recorded as "ship with width", then adopted
    unconditionally on the owner's rebuttal of the one argument against —
    the stale-ready escalation is period-scale, so nothing in the system
    leans on minute-scale oldest-first ordering. Urgent first, then random
    among the ready.
21. **"Tick" keeps its name for now** — the owner's naming rule (spell names
    out; no single nouns that need contextual reading) applies to everything
    new here ("the work step", "the readiness re-check at close", "heartbeat
    comments"), and renaming the tick itself is deferred to
    [#877](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/877) so it lands
    after the old slot scheduler's vocabulary retires and the
    "scheduler"-name collision is moot.
22. **One executor run performs one item — structurally** (§6, §10) —
    *amended 2026-08-15, same day*: first recorded as "`maxItems` defaults to
    one", then the knob deleted on the owner's correction ("An executor

    A run claims one item, sees it to its settle, and ends; a run ending

    the executor workflow carries a failure-continuation job — `needs:

    by the continuation + leash); stopping the *system* is a repo Actions
    variable every workflow checks as its first act, exiting having fired
    nothing. Items freeze untouched; resume is clearing the variable — the

content.text:
You're right, and the code is the stale side of that agreement.

**What's at line 157**

`engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs:157` is `for (let n = 0; n < maxItems; n += 1)` — one executor run draining up to `maxItems` items, defaulting to `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS = 3` (`executor.mjs:29`), overridable by `CLAUDINITE_MAX_ITEMS` at the CLI entry (`executor.mjs:499`).

**What was agreed**

`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` decision 22, "One executor run performs one item — structurally", amended the same day it was written: it was first recorded as "`maxItems` defaults to one", then the knob was **deleted** on your correction — *"An executor performs a task. It's not a current value. It's the essence of it."* A run claims one item, sees it to settle, and ends; a run ending with items still pickable re-dispatches a fresh run. The decision closes with the implementation note: *"(Engine: the `maxItems` surface deletes and the dispatch plumbing lands via #883.)"*

**Why it's still there**

[#883](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/883) is open and labelled `blocked` — it's the "engine still implements the pre-review contract" issue, and every box is unchecked, including **self-re-dispatch**. That box is what the loop is standing in for: without it, a run that ends after one item leaves the remaining queue waiting a full tick, and the two `continue` paths at lines 180 and 191 (lost claim, conflict revert) would burn a whole run doing nothing. So the deletion isn't independent — it's the same change as the dispatch plumbing, which is why neither has landed. Nothing about the loop is a considered dissent from the decision; it's just un-migrated.

The same issue also holds a second divergence in the same function: decision 20 adopted **randomized pick order** ("urgent first, then random among the ready"), but `pickOrder` still sorts urgent-then-oldest-created (`executor.mjs:68-71`), and the header comment at line 36 still describes oldest-first as the design.

Before I touch anything:

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. - extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.

content.text: Continue from where you left off.

You're right, and the code is out of date with the decision — it's not a design disagreement.

**What line 157 is:** `for (let n = 0; n < maxItems; n += 1)` in `runExecutor`, with `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS = 3` (`engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs:29`), overridable by `CLAUDINITE_MAX_ITEMS` at the CLI entry (`:499`).

**Why it's still there:** it's the *pre-review* contract. [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) decision 22 records exactly your point and your words:

> **One executor run performs one item — structurally** (§6, §10) — *amended 2026-08-15*: first recorded as "`maxItems` defaults to one", then the knob deleted on the owner's correction ("An executor performs a task. It's not a current value. It's the essence of it."). … (Engine: the `maxItems` surface deletes and the dispatch plumbing lands via #883.)

So the docs and the simulator carry "one run, one item"; `engine/scheduler/queue/` still carries the loop, deliberately parked behind [#883](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/883) (open, labelled `blocked`). The coupling is real: deleting the loop without the **self-re-dispatch** box from #883 means a run that finishes one item leaves the rest of the queue waiting a full tick each. That's why the two were scheduled together rather than the loop being deleted on its own.

Two related bits of the same drift, while I was in there:
- `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS = 3`, not 1 — so today a run can take three items, not even the interim "defaults to one".
- `pickOrder` still sorts urgent-then-oldest-created (`:68`), where decision 20 adopted **randomized** pick order among the ready. Same review, also unlanded.

Note the loop body's `continue` paths (lost claim, conflict revert) aren't concurrency — it's still strictly serial, one item at a time. The violation is that a *run* can do up to three, not that anything overlaps.

questions.question: The maxItems loop is the un-landed half of DESIGN decision 22, parked behind #883's self-re-dispatch. Land the deletion now, or keep it queued?

options.label: Land loop + re-dispatch together
options.description: Delete the maxItems surface (loop, constant, CLAUDINITE_MAX_ITEMS) and land the self-re-dispatch box from #883 in the same change, so a run that ends with pickable items dispatches a fresh run. This is the pairing the design assumes; the bigger of the options.

options.label: Delete the loop only
options.description: Remove maxItems now and accept that leftover items wait a tick each until #883's self-re-dispatch lands. Smaller change, matches the design's structural statement immediately, temporarily slower drains.

options.label: Leave it, tighten the record
options.description: No engine change; add a comment at line 157 naming decision 22 and #883 so the divergence is visible in the code, and leave the work in #883's queue.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

You're right — the loop contradicts the decision, and it's leftover code, not a design position.

**What was agreed.** [`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) decision 22: *"One executor run performs one item — structurally"*, amended the same day it was first written — it started as "`maxItems` defaults to one", and then the knob was deleted outright on your correction (*"An executor performs a task. It's not a current value. It's the essence of it."*). The decision's own parenthetical says: **"Engine: the `maxItems` surface deletes and the dispatch plumbing lands via #883."**

**What the code still has.** `engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs:157` is the pre-review contract, still shipping:
- `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS = 3` (`executor.mjs:29`), overridable by `CLAUDINITE_MAX_ITEMS` (`executor.mjs:499`);
- the module header comment still describes an executor as "a pull worker over the queue. **Each iteration**…";
- the comment at `executor.mjs:26-28` already argues the decision's own logic ("more capacity is more executors, not a longer loop") while keeping a 3-iteration loop.

Two of the loop's exits aren't the same thing as "a run does several tasks" — a lost claim (`continue`, `executor.mjs:181`) and a conflict revert (`executor.mjs:193`) both re-pick without having executed anything, which is the "move on to a DIFFERENT item" behaviour F15/F24 want. But `executor.mjs:196-201` genuinely executes an item and loops back for another, up to three. That's the part the decision deletes.

**Why it hasn't landed.** [#883](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/883) is the implementation issue and it's labelled `blocked` — it carries the whole work-as-work batch (heartbeat, tick/drain decoupling, durable record, readiness re-check at close, the `prework` rename), and the piece that has to land *with* the deletion is **self-re-dispatch**: without it, a run that drops to one item leaves the rest of the queue waiting a full tick each. So the loop is today's stand-in for drain-until-empty. Notably the deletion isn't spelled out as its own checkbox in #883's body — it's only in the DESIGN parenthetical, which is part of why it reads as un-tracked.

One adjacent divergence while I was in there: decision 20 adopted **randomized** pick order among the ready, and `pickOrder` (`executor.mjs:68-71`) still sorts oldest-created-first. Also un-landed, also not a checkbox anywhere.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

You're right, and the code is out of date with the decision — not deliberately.

**What line 157 is**

`engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs:157` is `for (let n = 0; n < maxItems; n += 1)`, with `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS = 3` at line 29 and a `CLAUDINITE_MAX_ITEMS` env override at line 499. Each iteration re-reads open items, picks one, claims it, and runs it to a settle — so it is serial, never concurrent, and two of its three `continue` paths (lost claim, conflict revert) end an iteration without executing anything. But it is still a run draining up to three items.

**What was agreed**

[`docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) decision 22:

> **One executor run performs one item — structurally** (§6, §10) — *amended 2026-08-15, same day*: first recorded as "`maxItems` defaults to one", then the knob deleted on the owner's correction ("An executor performs a task. It's not a current value. It's the essence of it.") … (Engine: the `maxItems` surface deletes and the dispatch plumbing lands via #883.)

So the deletion was agreed and explicitly deferred to [#883](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/883), which is still open and labelled `blocked`. The loop is the pre-review contract that #883 replaces: the *substitute* for it is self-re-dispatch (a run that ends with items still pickable `workflow_dispatch`es a fresh run), which is one of #883's unchecked boxes. Deleting the loop before that plumbing exists would make the queue drain one item per hourly tick — which is why the two are coupled in one issue rather than done separately.

Two related divergences in the same file, both from the same un-landed batch:
- `pickOrder` (line 68) still sorts **urgent, then oldest-created**; decision 20 adopted *urgent first, then random among the ready*.
- #883's own body doesn't list the `maxItems` deletion as a checkbox — only DESIGN §10 decision 22 records it, so the issue under-describes its own closing condition.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

{"number":801,"title":"Migration to the work-item queue: two PRs, one same-day validation burst","body":"The phase plan for [tasks-dispatch DESIGN](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md) (§14 points here). Design constraints from the owner (2026-08-13): **fewest disparate steps, fewest approval points, and certainty the same day** — we do not wait for a nightly run to learn whether the end state works. Deliberately generating real work to push traffic through every path is explicitly sanctioned.

**Approval points: two.** PR‑1 (mechanism + canon flip) and PR‑2 (fleet flip + slot deletion). Everything else is forcing and observing, which the mechanism itself defines as ordinary operations.

Checkboxes track progress; each burst row's checkbox is checked only with an evidence URL appended beside it.

---

## Where this stands (2026-08-16 12:10Z)

**One member is verified end to end, agentic lane included. Twelve more are blocked on owner-only credential work.** Steps 0–2 complete. Step 3 is most of the way: the flip is merged and observed, the first member ran a real agentic item to `outcome:done`, and three defects the burst could not have caught were found and two fixed. The slot deletion still waits on the remaining members.

| | state |
|---|---|
| Canon | on the queue since #854; 12 clean scheduler runs overnight, 12 items to terminal state |
| Fleet | flipped by default in #888 (`17902b9`); **GCEC verified end to end**, 12 members still need a CCR routine (#916) |
| Slot machinery | still in the tree, deliberately — deleting it before members are verified strands them (see Step 3) |
| Design vs engine | DESIGN/sim current to §15.24 plus F24; engine at pre-review behavior — the catch-up is Step 4 (#883) |
| Open follow-ups | #916 (owner-only, blocking), #921, #892, #924, #883, #877 |

## Step 0 — rehearsal (done)

- [x] Simulator + scenario suite green in CI; coverage map names the live-only rows

## Step 1 — PR‑1 on canon: the whole mechanism, canon flipped (approval №1)

- [x] Label vocabulary, tick workflow (cron + `workflow_dispatch`), executor workflow, janitor re-target, dependency fields + `after` yield + `create-work-item`, F8 signal exclusions, canon flipped, gate green
- [x] **Approval №1: PR‑1 merged** — #854, `b30ef77`

## Step 2 — the validation burst (complete)

- [x] **B1 creation + first-item rule (S25):** [run 31899008771](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31899008771) — 12 items #860–#870, each `task:blocked` wearing its next anchor
- [x] **B2 the roll + reasons on record (S1′):** #860 — one ask, rolled to tomorrow, reason on the item, no comment spam
- [x] **B3 agentic happy path + real CCR invocation + records (S2):** #867 — wake → claim → hand-off with nonce → **live session in 31s** → result + exec record → `outcome:done`
- [x] **B4 agentless path end to end:** #859 — wake → executor in 2s → claim → prework → `outcome:done`, closed in 26s, no session
- [x] **B5 the chain + yield (S4/S23):** #863 — yielded while `core/update` was live ([run 31913047785](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31913047785)), then claimed and running the moment the upstream cleared; its work merged as #887
- [x] ~~**B6 hourly cadence**~~ — **dropped** (owner). `create-extractor` is `gcec/create-extractor` on GoogleCalendarEventCreator, the fleet's only hourly task; canon has none
- [x] ~~**B7 missing-secret posture**~~ — **folded into Step 3** (owner): every member reaches the flip with its endpoint token unset, so the posture happens on real traffic with no scaffolding
- [x] **B8 force-while-executing mutex (S15):** #871 — queued behind the executing twin, then got its own verdict on release
- [x] **B9 multi-executor lease (S7):** #873 — three overlapping executors, exactly one claim, one execution
- [x] **B10 follow-up fields (S17):** #872 — `Blocked-by` + `Not-before` created and held blocked by the tick
- [x] **B11 janitor leashes:** [run 31900490000](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/31900490000) — 12 blocked/rolling items, zero escalations
- [x] **All burst rows green**

### What the burst caught that the rehearsal could not

Four defects, none of which any simulator would have produced. Three are fixed:

- **#879 → #881 (merged).** Hand-off appended a second `### Context` instead of replacing the first, splitting the item's binding scope while `instructions.md` says to read "the Context section", singular. Every unit test passed, because each tested one call. Confirmed fixed on live traffic in B5's own hand-off.
- **#882 → #885 (merged).** Queue sessions wrote `[unknown]` where the exec record's slot id used to go — `instructions.md` never said what replaces it — dropping the join from a record back to its work item.
- **The task-path guard fired correctly** on a hand-built item naming `task.mjs` instead of `task.md` (#871): refused, converged to `needs-human`, nothing run.
- **#892 (open).** The terminal convergence is agent-discretion, and **both** agentic runs got part of it wrong — #867's record field, and #863 closing with no outcome label and no exec record at all. Proposes a `converge-item.mjs` the session calls with its judged outcome.

## Step 3 — the fleet flip, then the deletion (approval №2)

**PR‑2 is two PRs, not one** (amendment, 2026-08-15). The plan said "slot machinery deleted in this same PR"; that is unsafe, and the reason is in the code:

- `updates/engine-update.mjs` **replaces the mount wholesale**, so a file canon deletes leaves every member's mount on its next converge whatever that member's config says.
- `.github/workflows/` is the one path a converge cannot push — staged, and landed later by the apply stage.
- The two stubs call **different entry points**: `run.mjs` vs `queue/tick.mjs`.

So deleting slots in the flip's own release strands any member whose workflow has not yet landed. Keeping the slot code makes that window benign (`run.mjs` no-ops) and #888 makes it **loud**.

- [x] The pack update flow staged only the scheduler workflow, so `claudinite-executor.yml` reached no member — #874, `5ca4c35`
- [x] **Approval №2: the flip merged** — #888, `17902b9`. `dispatchMode` answers `queue` for an absent setting, so members flip with **no edit to any file they own**
- [x] **A member's converge observed** — GoogleCalendarEventCreator, 2026-08-16 02:00:18–02:00:25Z: both stubs call the queue entry points out of the mount, `taskScheduler` carries no `dispatch` key, mount `queue/tick.mjs` byte-identical to canon HEAD, and [15 standing items created](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/918) (GCEC #904–#918). Last slot-era item was GCEC #903 at 00:09Z
- [x] **B7 lands here** — and the fault was **not** the unset secret the plan anticipated. `resolveEndpoint` fails at the *declaration*: [GCEC #908](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908#issuecomment-5305803329) parked `needs-human` naming `taskScheduler.endpoints`, no session started. `endpoints` was declared in exactly one repo in the fleet — this one — so the flip left **every** member's agentic lane dark
- [x] **Per-member mini-burst on the first member (B1–B4 + B7 + B3 agentic)** — GCEC: agentless lane ran clean from 02:00Z; [GCEC #908 closed `outcome:done` at 11:28:16Z](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/908) via a live session started 11:16:12Z, its work landing as GCEC #923; [GCEC #907 `core/update`](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/907) closed `outcome:done` 11:49:02Z, converging the mount through the queue itself
- [ ] **The other 12 members wired and observed** — blocked on #916 (owner-only: one CCR routine + `CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN` per repo)
- [ ] #921 folded in — DESIGN §8's force recipe yields an item `pickOrder` can never pick
- [ ] **Then** the slot deletion PR (slots.mjs, run-ledger math, exclusive claim, re-arm, `FORCE_TASKS` path, slot-conformance checks)
- [ ] The migration reports itself through the mechanism it ships: per-member fan-out items + a fan-in item `Blocked-by` all of them (S18 live) — fan-in closed `outcome:done`

### What Step 3 caught that Step 2 could not

Three defects, each invisible to the burst for a specific reason — and the reasons are the finding:

- **#906 → #907 (merged).** `queue/instructions.md` was never in the vendor set: `computeVendorSet` drops every `engine/**/*.md` behind a two-entry operational whitelist, and #854 added a third operational doc without extending it. That file *is* the behavior of a work-item session. **Invisible because canon runs the engine from its repo root, not a mount** — so no amount of canon traffic could show it.
- **#922 → #925 (merged).** F18's episode boundary was stated semantically and implemented over only the paths that already wrote a comment; the roll and the `needs-human` park end an episode silently, leaving a claim that outranks every future claimant. The roll self-heals via the leash (canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z); the park never does. Fixed by *striking* the claim — including on the **losing** claimant, whose claim would otherwise become the earliest of the next episode. **Invisible because the simulator modelled the rule's intent rather than its artifact**, so it was correct by construction; the sim now models the artifact and reproduces the bug without the fix.
- **#921 (open).** DESIGN §8's force recipe — strip `task:blocked`, optionally add `task:urgent` — omits `task:ready`, and `pickOrder` admits on `task:ready` alone. A forced item is invisible to every executor and the run logs `nothing ready to pick up`, which looks exactly like a healthy run. **Invisible because no executable artifact pins DESIGN's prose recipes.**

## Step 4 — the work-as-work engine catch-up (#883; starts only after Step 3's verification)

#884 (merged 2026-08-16, `4380639`) changed the design under the shipped mechanism — decisions §15.14–24. **The behavior-by-behavior checklist lives in #883** — one box per capability, each stating what breaks while it's off; this plan owns only the sequencing:

- [ ] **Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification** — the flip wave must be observed on the engine it shipped, not one changing underneath it
- [ ] Each #883 behavior lands burst-style per this plan's own discipline: a forced run observed on canon the same day; the workflow-touching pieces (heartbeat, decoupling, continuation job, suspend-all) additionally observed on one member's converge before the fleet's
- [ ] #892's `converge-item.mjs` is the natural carrier for #883's durable-record box — land them together, not twice
- [ ] #924 (a losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim) rides #883's heartbeat, which introduces the per-holder liveness signal it needs
- [ ] #877 (the tick rename) unblocks when this step closes — last, so the rename never churns files mid-migration

## Done means

- [x] All Step‑2 rows have evidence URLs on this issue
- [x] The first member flipped, wired and observed end to end — agentless and agentic
- [ ] All members flipped and observed; fan-in item closed `outcome:done`
- [ ] Slot machinery gone from the tree
- [ ] Step 4: the fielded engine matches DESIGN §15.14–24 — #883 closed
- [ ] 48h of ordinary operation as *confirmation* — explicitly not the proof; the burst was the proof

# Claudinite work-item executor (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6, §10) — a pull worker
# over the queue, triggered by a `task:ready` / `task:urgent` label event for
# latency and by hand for a drain. It carries NO cron: the tick's own drain job is
# the poll that makes a lost label event irrelevant, so events here are latency
# sugar and never the only delivery.
#
# THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE SECRETS LIVE (DESIGN §14). The wiring converge stamps
# every task's declared `required_secrets`, plus each configured invocation
# endpoint's token secret, into the step env below by name — the tick and the
# janitor get none, because they never execute task code. Code-work is the only task
# code that ever sees a value; the agent hop carries nothing.
#
# MORE CAPACITY IS MORE EXECUTORS. Nothing enumerates them and each claim is
# independently leased, so a second job, a matrix width, or a runner outside
# Actions entirely all work — the executor's whole interface is issue read/write
# plus the repo at HEAD.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A label event on anything else is not this workflow's business — and a
    # workflow_dispatch carries no label at all, so it always runs.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # MUST stay ≤ the engine's executing leash (60m): a hung runner has to be
    # killed by the platform before its claim is reaped and the item re-picked, or
    # a zombie's code-work runs beside its replacement's (F17).
    timeout-minutes: 50
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # Hand-maintained, like the tick beside it: the canon runs its own engine
          # at the repo root and no converge writes its workflows, so this list is
          # what the stub's `# claudinite:secrets` stamp produces on a member.
          FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
          CCR_FLEET_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_FLEET_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
        run: node engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs
============
# Claudinite work-item queue — the generator tick and its drain (tasks-dispatch
# DESIGN §5, §10). This is the repo's ONLY cron, and it replaces the slot
# scheduler's content at the same path when `taskScheduler.dispatch` is `"queue"`
# — same file, same hashed minute, different mechanism, so the one-cron rule and
# every reader that knows this workflow by name keep holding.
#
# A thin shim: all logic lives in the vendored engine, so this file changes
# rarely. The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap and the wiring converge
# rewrite it to this repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`.
#
# TWO JOBS, IN ORDER. The tick is pure label mechanics over the issue list —
# instantiate each task's standing item at its anchor, ready what is due, reclaim
# dead executor claims — and evaluates no precondition and collects no signal. The
# drain is an ordinary executor run: it picks up what the tick just created, which
# is what keeps the common case's latency at zero even with no `labeled` event
# delivered. Lost events are therefore never the only delivery — they are latency
# sugar, which is what retires the re-arm.
#
# `workflow_dispatch` is not a convenience: it is the never-wait-for-the-cron
# lever every forced run, migration and validation burst depends on. Its one
# input is how that lever reaches ACROSS repos: the fleet enforcer dispatches
# this workflow naming the tasks to run now, and this member wakes its own
# standing items with its own token (DESIGN §8). The alternative — the enforcer
# editing every member's issues directly — would widen the fleet PAT to issue
# writes on every repository, for a job the member can do for itself.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '44 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      wake:
        description: 'Task ids to run now (`pack/task` or a bare task name, space-separated) — wakes each one’s standing item regardless of its anchor'
        required: false
        type: string

# One tick at a time, always. The tick's duplicate-standing-item self-heal is
# written assuming exactly this — it closes every open family item but the oldest,
# which is safe precisely because two ticks never run at once.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-tick
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; a task's code_work pushes its delivery branch
  issues: write          # create / label / comment / close work items — the queue itself
  pull-requests: write   # a task's code_work opens its PR and arms auto-merge
  actions: write         # dispatch a workflow a task drives (creating a workflow_dispatch event needs write; `read` silently 403s the POST)

jobs:
  tick:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CLAUDINITE_WAKE: ${{ inputs.wake }}
        run: node engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs

  # The post-tick drain. `timeout-minutes` MUST stay ≤ the engine's executing
  # leash (60m): a hung runner has to be killed by the platform before its claim
  # is reaped and the item re-picked, or a zombie's code-work runs beside its
  # replacement's.
  drain:
    needs: tick
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 50
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Drain the queue
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # On a member this block is stamped by the wiring converge (the
          # `# claudinite:secrets` marker in the stub); the canon has no converge,
          # so its own list is written here, by hand, in the same commit.
          FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
          CCR_FLEET_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_FLEET_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
        run: node engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue. Converges to ONE open
  # issue by a fixed title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a
  # first-run failure may precede any label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: [tick, drain]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const title = 'Claudinite scheduler run failed';
            await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' }).catch(() => {});
            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${owner}/${repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
            const body = `The Claudinite tick/drain run failed: ${run}`;
            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels: ['workflow-failure'], body });

cron, rule unchanged — containing the tick job and a drain (the tick runs
first; the executor drains what it created, which keeps the common case's
latency at zero even without events). Event triggers (`task:ready` labeled)
give urgent and hand-created items sub-minute pickup — with one platform fact
worth knowing: a label written by a workflow's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` emits no
triggering event (GitHub's recursion guard), so events only ever come from
*foreign* tokens — a human, a CLI on a PAT, an agent session. The drain being
in-run is what makes that harmless; it is the structural delivery, events the
sugar.

**The capacity model, honestly** (work-as-work review, 2026-08-15): the work
step is the work, so throughput is run *occupancy* — one run, one item, and
the queue drains as a chain of runs. The CCR sessions runs hand off
parallelize for free; the executor-side work does not. So executor width is
the primary capacity parameter, not a garnish: scale with a matrix width for
parallel executor jobs, or with executors outside Actions entirely — the
contract is "issue read/write plus the repo checkout at HEAD", so a runner
anywhere with a token qualifies. The chain itself is **self-re-dispatch**:
`workflow_dispatch` is one of the two event types a `GITHUB_TOKEN` *can*
fire, so a run that ends with ready items left re-dispatches the executor
workflow and a fresh run continues.
One fairness note, accepted at today's scale: the randomized pick (§6.1)
removes any *systematic* head domination, but a heavy item still occupies its
run for the full work bound while light tasks wait out the chain — a sentence
here rather than machinery, until it is measured.

**What starts an executor run is an enumerable list, and each cause is on the
record** (2026-08-15, and the sim asserts it — S34): (1) **the tick's own
drain job** — the guaranteed delivery, started by the cron workflow's job
graph (`needs: tick`), no event involved; (2) **a `task:ready`/`task:urgent`
label event** — foreign tokens only, the latency sugar; (3) **the close-time
drain** — whoever converges an item triggers a drain when anything is
pickable after its readiness re-check (§9); (4) **self-re-dispatch** — a run
that ends its one item with others still pickable dispatches a fresh run;
(5) **the failure continuation** — a run that dies (crash, timeout,
cancellation, runner loss) never reaches its re-dispatch, so the executor
workflow carries a second job, `needs: execute` with `if: failure() ||
cancelled()`, which the platform runs on a fresh runner and whose one step
re-dispatches — a dead run stalls the train by ~a minute, not until the next
cron fire (S36). Causes 3–5 ride `workflow_dispatch`, which the default
`GITHUB_TOKEN` *is* permitted to fire — the explicit exemption in the same
recursion guard that suppresses its label events — so no wider credential is
involved.

content.content:
# Claudinite work-item executor (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6, §10) — a pull worker
# over the queue, triggered by a `task:ready` / `task:urgent` label event for
# latency and by hand for a drain. It carries NO cron: the tick's own drain job is
# the poll that makes a lost label event irrelevant, so events here are latency
# sugar and never the only delivery.
#
# THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE SECRETS LIVE (DESIGN §14). The wiring converge stamps
# every task's declared `required_secrets`, plus each configured invocation
# endpoint's token secret, into the step env below by name — the tick and the
# janitor get none, because they never execute task code. Code-work is the only task
# code that ever sees a value; the agent hop carries nothing.
#
# MORE CAPACITY IS MORE EXECUTORS. Nothing enumerates them and each claim is
# independently leased, so a second job, a matrix width, or a runner outside
# Actions entirely all work — the executor's whole interface is issue read/write
# plus the repo at HEAD.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A label event on anything else is not this workflow's business — and a
    # workflow_dispatch carries no label at all, so it always runs.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # MUST stay ≤ the engine's executing leash (60m): a hung runner has to be
    # killed by the platform before its claim is reaped and the item re-picked, or
    # a zombie's code-work runs beside its replacement's (F17).
    timeout-minutes: 50
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # The wiring converge stamps every declared required_secret, and every
          # configured invocation endpoint's token, below this marker — by name.
          # claudinite:secrets
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs
=== DIFF canon vs stub ===
51,57c51,54
<           # Hand-maintained, like the tick beside it: the canon runs its own engine
<           # at the repo root and no converge writes its workflows, so this list is
<           # what the stub's `# claudinite:secrets` stamp produces on a member.

# Claudinite work-item executor (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §6, §10) — a pull worker
# over the queue, triggered by a `task:ready` / `task:urgent` label event for
# latency and by hand for a drain. It carries NO cron: the tick's own drain job is
# the poll that makes a lost label event irrelevant, so events here are latency
# sugar and never the only delivery.
#
# THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE SECRETS LIVE (DESIGN §14). The wiring converge stamps
# every task's declared `required_secrets`, plus each configured invocation
# endpoint's token secret, into the step env below by name — the tick and the
# janitor get none, because they never execute task code. Code-work is the only task
# code that ever sees a value; the agent hop carries nothing.
#
# MORE CAPACITY IS MORE EXECUTORS. Nothing enumerates them and each claim is
# independently leased, so a second job, a matrix width, or a runner outside
# Actions entirely all work — the executor's whole interface is issue read/write
# plus the repo at HEAD.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A label event on anything else is not this workflow's business — and a
    # workflow_dispatch carries no label at all, so it always runs.
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # MUST stay ≤ the engine's executing leash (60m): a hung runner has to be
    # killed by the platform before its claim is reaped and the item re-picked, or
    # a zombie's code-work runs beside its replacement's (F17).

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # The wiring converge stamps every declared required_secret, and every
          # configured invocation endpoint's token, below this marker — by name.
          # claudinite:secrets
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs

import pathlib

"""

CONT = """
  # A run that dies — crash, timeout, cancellation, runner loss — never reaches
  # its own re-dispatch, so without this the queue would sit until the next cron
  # fire. The platform runs this job on a FRESH runner after any such death
  # (DESIGN §10, S36), and its one step fires that dispatch instead: the
  # remainder drains in ~a minute, while the dead run's OWN item waits for the
  # executing leash to reclaim it — nothing here touches that item.
  #
  # `continuation_depth` is the stop. A run that dies at startup — a broken
  # engine, a revoked token — dies identically every time, and an unguarded
  # continuation would dispatch itself for as long as that lasts; after three the
  # chain stops and the tick's own drain is the backstop, one hour out.
  continue-the-chain:
    needs: execute
    if: >-
      (failure() || cancelled())
      && fromJSON(inputs.continuation_depth || '0') < 3
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const depth = Number('${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}' || 0) + 1;
            const ref = context.payload.repository?.default_branch
              ?? context.ref.replace('refs/heads/', '');
            await github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              workflow_id: 'claudinite-executor.yml',
              ref,
              inputs: { continuation_depth: String(depth) },
            });
            core.info(`the executor run died — dispatched a fresh one on ${ref} (continuation ${depth} of 3)`);
"""

    assert INPUT_BLOCK in s, path
    s = s.replace(INPUT_BLOCK, INPUT_NEW, 1)
    assert not s.endswith('\n\n')
    s = s.rstrip('\n') + '\n' + CONT

input.head: claude/executor-loop-question-nyfelg
input.body:
The first slice of #883's engine catch-up: the run-shape decisions (DESIGN §15.20, §15.22, §15.23), which are what the executor's own `for` loop contradicted.

## What changes

**`maxItems` deletes.** `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS`, `CLAUDINITE_MAX_ITEMS` and the loop in `runExecutor` are gone. A run claims one item, sees it to its settle, and ends — structural, not a number to raise (§15.22: *"An executor performs a task. It's not a current value. It's the essence of it."*).

**The chain replaces the loop.** A run that settled its item re-reads the queue and, if anything is still pickable, `workflow_dispatch`es the executor workflow — the exemption in the same recursion guard that suppresses `GITHUB_TOKEN` label events, so no wider credential. A run that settled *nothing* dispatches nothing: re-dispatching after a lost race argues with the executor that won, and after a claim revert it is two executors dispatching each other.

**The workflow gains a failure-continuation job** (§15.23): `needs: execute`, `if: failure() || cancelled()`, one step that re-dispatches from a fresh runner, so a run that dies before reaching its own dispatch stalls the queue by ~a minute rather than an hour. It carries a `continuation_depth` input capped at 3 — a run that dies *at startup* dies identically every time, and an unguarded continuation would dispatch itself for as long as that lasts. Beyond three, the tick's own drain is the backstop.

**Pick order randomizes** (§15.20): urgent first, then random among the ready. With one item per run, a deterministic order lets one unlucky head dominate a whole chain.

## Not in this PR

The rest of #883 — heartbeat, the `timeout-minutes ≤ leash` retirement, tick/drain decoupling, the durable record, the readiness re-check at close, the operator hold, the `prework` rename. Boxes and sequencing are on #883.

## Verification

- Full suite: 2268 pass, 0 fail. `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking (64 advisory, all pre-existing in packs this PR doesn't touch).
- See-it-fail: the four new run-shape tests were run against the pre-change engine (`git checkout HEAD^ -- executor.mjs`) and fail there; the two pick-order property tests fail against the old oldest-first comparator.
- Not yet observed on a live run — #801's Step 4 discipline asks for a forced run on canon the same day, and the continuation job additionally on one member's converge. That is the next step, not something this diff can claim.

## Folders touched

- **`engine/scheduler/queue/`** — `executor.mjs`: the loop deletes, `pickOrder` randomizes with an injectable draw, `runExecutor` gains a `redispatch` seam and the CLI wires it.
- **`engine/scheduler/`** — `github.mjs`: `dispatchWorkflow`, status-checked; `signals/gh.mjs`: `EXECUTOR_WORKFLOW_FILE` beside the scheduler's.
- **`engine/scheduler/stubs/` + `.github/workflows/`** — the continuation job and its `continuation_depth` input, both copies, diffed against each other (they differ only in the secrets block and the entry path, as before).

Refs #883

Three decisions from the same review have no box on this issue — each was recorded only in a comment (or nowhere), and two of them are what a session reading `executor.mjs` trips over first. Adding them to the checklist, and marking what #1089 lands.

- [x] **The `maxItems` surface deletes** (§15.22) — `DEFAULT_MAX_ITEMS`, `CLAUDINITE_MAX_ITEMS` and the loop in `runExecutor`; a run performs one item, structurally. This was only ever in a comment above, whose *first* half ("defaults to one") was superseded 30 minutes later — so the body's checklist folded it into "self-re-dispatch" and the number stayed 3. While off: the executor's own header comment argues against its own loop, and every reader has to reconstruct which comment won. — #1089
- [x] **Randomized pick order** (§15.20) — `pickOrder` still sorts oldest-created. Not a box anywhere, not mentioned in the body. While off: harmless under a multi-item loop, but with one item per run a deterministic head dominates the whole chain — the exposure the decision was taken to remove. — #1089
- [x] **The failure-continuation job** (§15.23) — a comment above, never a body box. While off: a run that dies mid-work stalls the queue until the next cron. — #1089 (with a `continuation_depth` cap of 3, which the decision did not specify: a run that dies at startup dies identically every time, and an unguarded continuation dispatches itself for as long as that lasts)
- [ ] **Tests that encode the pre-review contract** — `engine-tests/scheduler/queue/executor-loop.test.mjs` asserted `the loop stops at maxItems`, and `executor-rules.test.mjs` asserted oldest-first. Rewritten in #1089; noting the class here because the remaining boxes have the same exposure — a green suite is no evidence the engine matches the design.

The `blocked` label stands on its own terms: #801 Step 4 waits for Step 3's per-member verification, which waits on #916 (owner-only). #1089 is the engine-side slice that needs no member to be wired; the boxes that touch a member's workflow (heartbeat, decoupling, the suspend-all gate) still want that verification first.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, name the folders the change touched** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Leave out test folders, README edits, and above all any file whose diff is comments only.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. - extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). You are auditing the status of a tracking issue in the repo at /home/user/Claudinite (GitHub: missingbulb/Claudinite). Read-only: DO NOT edit files, DO NOT post comments, DO NOT push. Report your findings as text back to me.

CONTEXT
- Issue #883 "queue engine: implement the work-as-work amendments" is the engine catch-up for the tasks-dispatch design review. Its checklist is in the issue body; three more decisions live in its comments; I just added a comment (issue comment id 5354126267) adding three boxes.
- The authoritative design is docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md (decisions in §15, numbered; §6, §9, §10, §11, §14 are the mechanism sections). The simulator docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/scenarios.test.mjs pins expected behavior in scenarios S1–S38.
- The engine lives in engine/scheduler/ (queue/ especially: executor.mjs, tick.mjs, prework-run.mjs, leases.mjs, janitor-rules.mjs, create-work-item.mjs, invoke.mjs, code-work-run.mjs). Workflows: .github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml, .github/workflows/claudinite-executor.yml, and their stubs in engine/scheduler/stubs/.
- PR #1089 (branch claude/executor-loop-question-nyfelg, currently checked out) just landed three of the boxes in the working tree: maxItems deletion / one-item-per-run, self-re-dispatch, randomized pick order, failure-continuation job. Treat those as done-in-this-branch, and verify they are actually complete and consistent with the design rather than assuming.

WHAT I NEED, box by box. The #883 checklist boxes are:
1. Heartbeat comments (executor comments on the item every ~15 min during the work step; the tick's leash reclaim measures heartbeat silence)
2. Retire the `timeout-minutes <= leash` comments in both workflows once the heartbeat lands; size run timeouts appropriately
3. Tick/drain decoupling (the drain job leaving the claudinite-tick concurrency group)
4. Self-re-dispatch
5. Durable record (terminal comment carries the claudinite-task-exec record + artifact links)
6. Readiness re-check at close (F1) — executor/agent close paths ready dependents, then trigger a drain
7. Rename the `prework` contract key to the design's "work step" vocabulary (a fleet migration)
Plus from comments: the operator hold CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL (§15.24), the failure-continuation job (§15.23), randomized pick order (§15.20), maxItems deletion (§15.22).
Also related open issues named on #883/#801: #892 (converge-item.mjs), #921 (force recipe omits task:ready), #924 (losing claimant's comment defers the leash reclaim), #877 (tick rename), #916 (owner-only CCR routine wiring, blocking).

For EACH box report:
(a) STATUS against the current working tree: not started / partially present / already done. Cite file:line evidence for anything you claim is present. A grep miss is not evidence of absence — read the plausible files.
(b) The DECISION as the design actually states it: quote or cite the DESIGN.md section/decision number and the sim scenario that pins it. Flag any place where the issue's checklist text, an issue comment, and DESIGN.md DISAGREE with each other — that is the most valuable thing you can find. Also flag any decision that was superseded by a later one (several were amended the same day, 2026-08-15/16).
(c) DEPENDENCIES: what must land before it, and whether it touches only the engine (converges to members nightly) or also a member's workflow file (needs the wiring converge / a member observed).
(d) Any box that is now WRONG or MOOT because of later changes to the tree (e.g. a retired mechanism, a renamed module, a decision reversed).

Use the GitHub MCP tools (mcp__github__*) to read issues #883, #801, #892, #921, #924, #916, #877 including their comments. Use git log/git show for history. Be concrete and terse; I want a per-box table-like report plus a "contradictions found" section. Do not speculate where you can read.

lastPrompt: Explain again what's needed for 883, tell me how to help, and start working on it. Add the other divergences to be fixed too.
